ble_219_0c05d0c4.name: ble_sched_check_and_pend_pendsv
ble_219_0c05d0c4.summary: Request a PendSV exception when the scheduler object reports pending work
ble_219_0c05d0c4.description: Calls the status query at 0x0C042988 on the scheduler object at DAT_20017184 with flag 1 and a local out-word. If the out-word comes back non-zero it writes 0x10000000 to SCB->ICSR (0xE000ED04), the PENDSVSET bit, so the RTOS context switch runs once no higher-priority exception is active. It has no effect when the out-word is zero and does not clear any pending state itself. It has no direct callers in the packet, so it is reached through an indirect call or a table.
ble_219_0c05d0c4.notes: The status routine 0x0C042988 and the object type of DAT_20017184 are not described yet, so the meaning of the out-word is inferred from the PendSV write.

ble_219_0c05d2f4.name: ble_xfer_pump_chunk_and_notify
ble_219_0c05d2f4.summary: Move one chunk of a pending transfer under a lock and signal the scheduler
ble_219_0c05d2f4.description: Takes the lock object at 0x2001722C (0x0C0431F8 with timeout 0xFFFFFFFF, i.e. wait forever). If the u16 remaining count at 0x2001728C is non-zero it asks 0x0C045518 how many bytes it can take from the cursor word at 0x20017288, subtracts that from the remaining count, advances the cursor by the same amount and sets the flag word at 0x20017298 to 1. It then releases the lock (0x0C042DF4) and signals event 1 on the scheduler object at 0x20017184 through ble_sched_signal_event. When nothing is left it only releases the lock.
ble_219_0c05d2f4.notes: The chunk routine 0x0C045518 and the buffer behind the cursor are not described yet. The lock semantics are inferred from the wait-forever timeout argument.

ble_219_0c05d494.name: ble_sched_signal_event
ble_219_0c05d494.summary: Signal event 1 on the BLE scheduler object at 0x20017184
ble_219_0c05d494.description: Thin wrapper that calls the event-set primitive at 0x0C04291C with the object pointer DAT_20017184 and event number 1. It is the same signal that ble_xfer_pump_chunk_and_notify issues after moving a chunk, so it is used to wake the BLE task when work becomes ready. Its caller 0x0C05AE14 is not described yet.

ble_219_0c05e2c0.name: wc_AesGcmEncrypt
ble_219_0c05e2c0.summary: Validate AES-GCM encrypt arguments, then run the software GCM encrypt
ble_219_0c05e2c0.description: wolfSSL wc_AesGcmEncrypt argument check. It rejects a NULL context (first argument), a zero IV length (sixth argument) and an authentication tag size outside 12..16 (eighth argument, tested as (size - 12) < 5 unsigned), returning BAD_FUNC_ARG (-173, 0xFFFFFF53). Otherwise it tail-calls the software CTR plus GHASH implementation at 0x0C05DE8C (AES_GCM_encrypt_C), which produces the ciphertext and the authentication tag. The data and IV pointers are not checked here.

params.name: param_1
params.description: wolfSSL Aes context, must be non-NULL

returns.description: result of the software encrypt, or -173 (BAD_FUNC_ARG) for invalid arguments

ble_219_0c05e2c0.notes: The 6th and 8th arguments are read from the stack at offsets 0x4 and 0xC, which the decompiler does not declare. The mapping follows the AAPCS stack layout.

ble_219_0c05e420.name: GetInt
ble_219_0c05e420.summary: Parse one ASN.1 DER INTEGER at an index and load it into a big integer
ble_219_0c05e420.description: wolfSSL asn.c GetInt. GetASNInt (0x0C05E3B8) reads the INTEGER header at input[*idx], skips a leading 0x00 pad byte and returns the content length. The destination is then mp_init()ed and the magnitude is loaded big-endian with mp_read_unsigned_bin (reached through a thunk at 0x0C062BAC). On success *idx is advanced by header plus content length and 0 is returned. If the load fails the integer is cleared with fp_clear; the error paths return -142 (ASN parse error) or -110 (mp_init failure). The value is always non-negative because the sign is not decoded.

params.name: param_3
params.description: in/out byte index into the input

returns.description: 0 on success, -110 on mp_init failure, -142 on parse or load failure

ble_219_0c05e474.name: DecodeECC_DSA_Sig
ble_219_0c05e474.summary: Parse a DER ECDSA signature SEQUENCE into its r and s integers
ble_219_0c05e474.description: wolfSSL DecodeECC_DSA_Sig. It requires the first byte to be 0x30 (SEQUENCE tag), reads the SEQUENCE length with GetLength_ex (0x0C05E350) and checks that it fits the buffer. It then decodes two consecutive INTEGERs with GetInt (0x0C05E420), the first into r (param_3) and the second into s (param_4). If anything fails it clears r with fp_clear and returns -171 (0xFFFFFF55). Returns 0 when both integers parse.
ble_219_0c05e474.notes: The wolfSSL identification is inferred from the SEQUENCE plus two INTEGER structure and the argument order.

ble_219_0c05e614.name: wc_ecc_curve_load
ble_219_0c05e614.summary: Load selected fields of a standard ECC curve into an ecc_curve_spec
ble_219_0c05e614.description: wolfSSL wc_ecc_curve_load. A NULL curve returns BAD_FUNC_ARG (-173). The spec stores the new curve pointer at +0x00, and if the same curve was already loaded it keeps the fields already present. For each requested field bit in load_mask it takes the next fp_int slot from the pool (slot size 0x68, pool base at +0x18, count at +0x1C, used count at +0x20), runs mp_init on it and parses the curve's hex constant with fp_read_radix(..., 16). The loaded-field mask is stored at +0x24. When the pool is exhausted it returns -170 or -340. Other failures free the spec with wc_ecc_curve_free (0x0C05E4E8) and return -111.

params.name: param_3
params.description: load_mask, one bit per curve field (prime, A, B, order, Gx, Gy)

returns.description: 0 on success, -173 for a NULL curve, -170 or -340 on pool exhaustion, -111 on load failure

ble_219_0c05e614.notes: The bit-to-field mapping is inferred from the slot assignments. Bit 2 is not tested by the decompiled branches, so one field may be loaded through a path not seen here.

ble_219_0c062f28.name: fp_div_2d
ble_219_0c062f28.summary: Divide a big integer by 2^b giving quotient and optional remainder
ble_219_0c062f28.description: wolfSSL TFM fp_div_2d: c = a >> b and, when d is non-NULL, d = a mod 2^b. For b <= 0 it copies a to c and clears d. Otherwise it copies a to c, computes the remainder with fp_mod_2d (0x0C0624E8) from the original a before shifting, shifts whole 32-bit digits with fp_rshd (0x0C062E40) when b >= 32, shifts the remaining bits with fp_rshb (0x0C062EA8), and trims leading zero digits from the result. Uses newlib memcpy and memset for the copies.

ble_219_0c064088.name: fp_add_thunk
ble_219_0c064088.summary: Branch-only alias of fp_add (signed big-integer addition)
ble_219_0c064088.description: Single-instruction thunk that branches to fp_add at 0x0C061FE8; the decompiled body shown is the target's. Called from ble_219_0c05f8c4 and ble_219_0c060828.

params.name: param_4
params.description: extra argument passed through to the helper

ble_219_0c06408c.name: fp_sub_thunk
ble_219_0c06408c.summary: Branch-only alias of fp_sub (signed big-integer subtraction)
ble_219_0c06408c.description: Single-instruction thunk that branches to fp_sub at 0x0C062068; the decompiled body shown is the target's. Called from ble_219_0c060828.

ble_219_0c0640e4.name: fp_submod_ct_thunk
ble_219_0c0640e4.summary: Branch-only alias of fp_submod_ct (constant-time modular subtraction)
ble_219_0c0640e4.description: Single-instruction thunk that branches to fp_submod_ct at 0x0C0625A0; the decompiled body shown is the target's. It computes d = (a - b) mod c in constant time. Called from ble_219_0c05e868 and ble_219_0c05eb00.

params.name: param_2
params.description: modulus c, passed through to the helper

ble_219_0c0640e8.name: fp_addmod_ct_thunk
ble_219_0c0640e8.summary: Branch-only alias of fp_addmod_ct (constant-time modular addition)
ble_219_0c0640e8.description: Single-instruction thunk that branches to fp_addmod_ct at 0x0C062654; the decompiled body shown is the target's. It computes d = (a + b) mod c in constant time. Called from ble_219_0c05e868 and ble_219_0c05eb00.

params.name: param_2
params.description: modulus c, passed through to the helper

ble_219_0c064284.name: fp_rshb_thunk
ble_219_0c064284.summary: Branch-only alias of fp_rshb (in-place right shift by bits)
ble_219_0c064284.description: Single-instruction thunk that branches to fp_rshb at 0x0C062EA8; the decompiled body shown is the target's. It shifts the big integer right in place by the given number of bits, after whole-digit shifts for counts of 32 or more. Called from ble_219_0c0601fc.

ble_219_0c064288.name: fp_montgomery_calc_normalization_thunk
ble_219_0c064288.summary: Branch-only alias of fp_montgomery_calc_normalization (R mod b)
ble_219_0c064288.description: Single-instruction thunk that branches to fp_montgomery_calc_normalization at 0x0C062940; the decompiled body shown is the target's. It computes a = R mod b, with R = 2^(32 * used digits of b), by repeated doubling and conditional subtraction, for Montgomery normalisation. Called from ble_219_0c05b724 and ble_219_0c05e558.

params.name: param_4
params.description: fallback word used when b is a single digit

returns.description: 0 on success, or the error code from the doubling helper

ble_219_0c064498.name: fp_div_2_mod_ct_thunk
ble_219_0c064498.summary: Branch-only alias of fp_div_2_mod_ct (constant-time halving modulo b)
ble_219_0c064498.description: Single-instruction thunk that branches to fp_div_2_mod_ct at 0x0C062450; the decompiled body shown is the target's. It computes c = (a / 2) mod b for 0 <= a < b: when a is odd it adds b first, then halves the result, in constant time. Called from ble_219_0c05e868 and ble_219_0c05eb00.

ble_219_0c065148.name: ble_host_hci_init_once
ble_219_0c065148.summary: One-time setup of the HCI event state that registers the packet handler
ble_219_0c065148.description: Runs once: if the init byte at 0x20017385 is already non-zero it returns. Otherwise it sets that byte to 1, stores the handler address 0x0C064C6C (Thumb 0x0C064C6D) at 0x20017394, calls hci_add_event_handler (0x0C066DBC) to register it on the event-handler list at env+0x20, and clears the state words at 0x200172DC, 0x20017300, 0x2001738C and 0x20017388 to zero.
ble_219_0c065148.notes: The decompile drops the arguments of the hci_add_event_handler call. The registered handler is assumed to be the one stored at 0x20017394.

ble_219_0c066370.name: ble_ctrl_conn_free_guarded
ble_219_0c066370.summary: Free a connection record only when its state byte is 1 or 2
ble_219_0c066370.description: Guard in front of the disconnect path. It returns at once unless the connection state byte at +0x0E is 1 or 2 (tested as (state - 1) > 1). Otherwise it runs the same sequence as ble_ctrl_conn_free_and_report_disconnect (0x0C06637A): unlink the record from the list at env+0x14 (btstack_linked_list_remove, 0x0C06542C), return it to the pool (btstack_memory_hci_connection_free, 0x0C0654E4), emit the 9-byte event 0xD9 0x07 with the reason byte and the reversed peer address when bit 15 of the flags word at +0x10 is set, and when the reason is 5 call the interface callback at env+0x10 offset +0x14 with the address.
ble_219_0c066370.notes: The packet lists 0x0C06637A as the callee, but Ghidra shows the body inline here. The meaning of reason 5 is unconfirmed, as in 0x0C06637A.

ble_219_0c06648c.name: ble_ctrl_disconnect_all_connections
ble_219_0c06648c.summary: Disconnect every connection with reason 0x16 and tear each one down
ble_219_0c06648c.description: Walks the connection list at env+0x14 with a removal-safe iterator. For each connection it builds a 6-byte HCI Disconnection Complete event (05 04 00 handle_lo handle_hi 16) with the handle from +0x0A and reason 0x16 (Connection Terminated By Local Host), emits it with hci_emit_event (0x0C066004, length 6), then calls ble_ctrl_conn_teardown_and_count (0x0C0663E8) to stop its timers, unlink and free it and emit the count event. Callers are ble_219_0c0674e8 and ble_219_0c06b154.

ble_219_0c066a4c.name: ll_env_can_send_acl
ble_219_0c066a4c.summary: Report whether ACL data can be sent, unless the env busy byte at 0x170 is set
ble_219_0c066a4c.description: If the busy byte at env+0x170 is non-zero (the byte ll_env_is_ready also tests) it returns 0. Otherwise it returns the result of ble_ctrl_can_send_to_handle (0x0C0669D8), which reports whether the connection has free ACL slots. The decompiled call shows no arguments, so the handle is the value the caller left in the argument registers.

returns.description: 0 while the busy byte is set, otherwise the free-ACL-slot result (non-zero when a slot is free)

ble_219_0c06d5c4.name: ll_env_can_send_acl_thunk
ble_219_0c06d5c4.description: One-instruction thunk that branches to 0x0C066A4C, with the same body. It is called from ble_219_0c04def0 and ble_219_0c051eb8.

ble_219_0c066f74.name: ble_ctrl_hci_cmd_dispatch
ble_219_0c066f74.summary: Apply a host HCI command to the controller state, then forward it to the transport hook
ble_219_0c066f74.description: Reads the opcode (u16 at offset 0) and dispatches on it. Opcode 0x0429 stores the u16 at offset 0x13 in env+0x1D2 and the 6-byte peer address at offset 3, reversed, in env+0x239, with address type 0xFC at env+0x23F. Opcode 0x0428 stores the u16 at offset 0x0F in env+0x1D2. Opcode 0x1802 stores the byte at offset 3 in env+0x75. Opcode 0x0405 is the create-connection path: the peer address is compared with the local address at env+0x0E (memcmp), a match emits a Connection Complete event (0x03, length 11) with status 0x0F, and otherwise a record of type 0xFD is found (ble_ctrl_conn_find_by_addr) or allocated (ble_ctrl_conn_alloc_and_register, status 0x56 on failure) and put in state 1. Every path decrements the pending-command counter at env+0x177, calls ble_hook_invoke4 (0x0C06C0C0) with hook id 1, then calls the transport hook at *env+0x18 with (1, command, length). The return value is 0 when the hook accepts and 3 otherwise.

params.name: param_1
params.description: HCI command buffer, opcode u16 at +0, parameters from +3

returns.description: HCI status: 0 accepted, 3 transport hook refused, or an error status (0x0B, 0x0F, 0x56) from an opcode handler

ble_219_0c066f74.notes: The meaning of the stored env fields at 0x1D2, 0x239, 0x23F and 0x75 is inferred from the writes. The status constants are taken from the Connection Complete and HCI status codes.

ble_219_0c067178.name: hci_send_cmd
ble_219_0c067178.summary: Reserve the HCI packet buffer and send one command, or report that it is busy
ble_219_0c067178.description: BTstack hci_send_cmd. If the controller is not ready (ll_env_is_ready, 0x0C066978) it logs 'hci_send_cmd called but cannot send packet now' (hci.c line 0x1C6C) and returns 0x0C (Command Disallowed). Otherwise it stores the opcode in env+0x1AE. If the packet-buffer-reserved byte at env+0x170 is already set it logs 'hci_reserve_packet_buffer called but buffer already reserved' (line 0x2F5) and 'hci_host_num_completed_packets, hci packet buffer reserved' (line 0x1C76), then returns 0x0C. Otherwise it sets the reserved byte, packs the command with hci_cmd_pack_format (0x0C06BC74), and dispatches it through ble_ctrl_hci_cmd_dispatch (0x0C066F74). On success it returns 0. On failure it clears the reserved byte, emits a 2-byte internal event 0x6E through hci_emit_event and returns the error.

returns.description: 0 when the command was accepted, 0x0C when it cannot be sent now, or the dispatch error

ble_219_0c06722c.name: hci_send_cmd_no_status
ble_219_0c06722c.summary: Send an HCI command through hci_send_cmd and discard its status
ble_219_0c06722c.description: Calls hci_send_cmd (0x0C067178) with the same argument and ignores its return value. Callers are ble_219_0c051eb8, ble_219_0c06464c, ble_219_0c065038, ble_219_0c067248, ble_219_0c0674e8, ble_219_0c068cc8 and ble_219_0c06cdb8.

params.name: param_1
params.description: command descriptor passed through to hci_send_cmd

ble_219_0c06d474.name: l2cap_channel_pool_init
ble_219_0c06d474.summary: Initialise the L2CAP channel pool header, CID counter and channel handlers
ble_219_0c06d474.description: Sets up the L2CAP state at 0x2001944C. It writes 0x40 to the local CID counter at 0x200194A4 (the first dynamic CID used by l2cap_create_channel_entry) and 0xFF to 0x200194B4. It writes four (u16, u16) pairs into the record: (1, 2) at +0x0C/+0x0E, (4, 7) at +0x1C/+0x1E, (3, 4) at +0x2C/+0x2E and (3, 6) at +0x3C/+0x3E, and links the record with btstack_linked_list_add (0x0C0653EC) each time. It stores 0x0C06E7D0 at 0x20019498 as a channel callback and 0x0C06DC50 at env+0x18 as the transport hook, then registers the packet handler with hci_add_event_handler (0x0C066DBC).
ble_219_0c06d474.notes: Reading the pairs as fixed-channel or protocol IDs is inferred, not confirmed. The callback and hook targets are taken from the stored addresses.

ble_219_0c06f220.name: sqrt
ble_219_0c06f220.summary: Double square root with domain check: returns NaN and sets EDOM for negative input
ble_219_0c06f220.description: newlib sqrt wrapper (w_sqrt). It computes __ieee754_sqrt (0x0C06F2CC) on the argument. If the argument is not NaN (__unorddf2) and is less than zero (__aeabi_dcmplt against 0.0) it sets errno to 0x21 (EDOM) through __errno and returns NaN, computed as 0/0 with __aeabi_ddiv. Otherwise it returns the __ieee754_sqrt result.

params.name: param_1
params.description: low word of the double argument

params.name: param_2
params.description: high word of the double argument

returns.description: IEEE double square root in r0:r1, or NaN for negative input

ble_219_0c06f2cc.name: __ieee754_sqrt
ble_219_0c06f2cc.description: Soft-float IEEE double square root in the fdlibm style. Inf and NaN return x*x + x (__aeabi_dmul then __aeabi_dadd). Negative finite input returns (x - x) / (x - x) (__aeabi_dsub then __aeabi_ddiv), which is NaN. Otherwise it normalises the mantissa and computes the root one bit at a time, with a 22-step loop for the high digits and a 32-step loop for the low digits, keeping the restoring remainder in a register pair, then rounds the last bit.

returns.description: square root in d0; the decompiler shows only the low word

ble_219_0c06f2cc.notes: The argument arrives in d0, which the decompiler shows as an implicit input. The result is correct for the branches that the callees identify.

ble_219_0c071618.name: sscanf
ble_219_0c071618.summary: Parse values from a NUL-terminated string with a scanf format
ble_219_0c071618.description: Newlib sscanf. It builds a string-backed FILE on the stack with read flags 0x204, _file set to -1, the buffer set to the string, the size set to strlen of the string (0x0C071756), and the end-of-file read stub at 0x0C071692. It then calls __ssvfiscanf_r (0x0C0728B0) on the impure reent (DAT_200049A8) with the format and the variadic argument list.

returns.description: number of assigned fields from __ssvfiscanf_r, which the decompile does not capture

ble_219_0c071a70.name: _gettimeofday_r
ble_219_0c071a70.summary: Reentrant gettimeofday wrapper that copies a failure errno into the reent
ble_219_0c071a70.description: Newlib _gettimeofday_r style wrapper. It clears the errno scratch word at 0x20019540, calls gettimeofday (0x0C0400CC, the FreeRTOS tick plus the epoch offset), and if that returns -1 with a non-zero scratch errno it stores the scratch value into the first word of the impure reent (DAT_200049A8), which is _errno.

ble_219_0c0723ec.name: setenv
ble_219_0c0723ec.summary: Front end for setenv: look up NAME in environ with the impure reent
ble_219_0c0723ec.description: Newlib-style setenv(name, value, overwrite) front end. It keeps value and overwrite in stack slots and calls the environ lookup _findenv_r (0x0C072404) with the impure reent (DAT_200049A8), the name and the stack slots by address. The decompiled call has five arguments, so the lifted argument list is unreliable and this is only the best reading of the setenv entry point.
ble_219_0c0723ec.notes: Low confidence: the wrapper body does not show the full setenv logic and the argument mapping is inconsistent. It may be getenv-related.

ble_219_0c07247c.name: _setenv_r
ble_219_0c07247c.summary: Reentrant setenv front end: look up NAME in environ and pass the result on
ble_219_0c07247c.description: Same shape as setenv (0x0C0723EC) but takes the reent pointer as its first argument. It calls the environ lookup _findenv_r (0x0C072404) with (reent, name, a stack slot holding the value, param_4, reent) and returns nothing in the decompile.
ble_219_0c07247c.notes: Low confidence for the same reason as setenv: the four-argument call is lifted with five words, so the mapping of the arguments is inferred.

ble_219_0c086e08.name: norflash_erase_range
ble_219_0c086e08.summary: Erase a byte range of a flash slot with 4 KiB, 32 KiB or whole-chip erases
ble_219_0c086e08.description: Checks the start address against the slot size at 0x20003568 + id*0x24 (returns 0x0B if the start is out of range, 0x0C if the length runs past the end) and rounds the start down and the end up to 4 KiB. It calls norflash_pre_operation (0x0C088858), then erases: if the range covers the whole chip it issues one whole-chip norflash_erase (kind 4, 0x0C088F20); otherwise it issues 4 KiB sector erases (kind 1) until the address is 32 KiB aligned, 32 KiB block erases (kind 2) while at least 0x8000 bytes remain, and 4 KiB erases for the tail. norflash_post_operation (0x0C0888D8) runs at the end. If an erase reports 1 (suspended), the progress is saved in 0x20003598[id] (address) and 0x200035A8[id] (remaining length), the state byte at 0x200035B0[id] is set to 2, and the function returns 1.

params.name: param_4
params.description: extra argument passed to the flash operations

returns.description: 0 when complete, 1 when suspended with progress saved, 0x0B or 0x0C for a bad range, otherwise the error from the erase

ble_219_0c086e08.notes: The erase kind mapping (1 = 4 KiB, 2 = 32 KiB, 4 = whole chip) comes from norflash_erase (0x0C088F20).

ble_219_0c086f38.name: norflash_program_range
ble_219_0c086f38.summary: Program a byte range of a flash slot page by page, with suspend and resume state
ble_219_0c086f38.description: Checks the start address against the slot size at 0x20003568 + id*0x24 (returns 0x0B) and that the length fits (returns 0x0C). It then programs in pieces that stop at page boundaries, each no larger than the page size at 0x2000356C + id*0x24, by calling norflash_page_program (0x0C089064) and advancing the flash address, the source buffer and the remaining length. norflash_pre_operation and norflash_post_operation bracket the loop. A suspended result (1) saves the address, buffer and remaining length in 0x20003598, 0x200035A0 and 0x200035A8 (indexed by id) and sets the state byte at 0x200035B0[id] to 4.

params.name: param_5
params.description: extra argument passed to the page program

returns.description: 0 when complete, 1 when suspended with progress saved, 0x0B or 0x0C for a bad range, otherwise the page-program error

ble_219_0c0873ec.name: norflash_slot_op_locked
ble_219_0c0873ec.summary: Run a flash slot callback with the flash bracketed and interrupts masked
ble_219_0c0873ec.description: Rejects an id above 1, or a slot whose initialised flag at 0x20003550[id*0x24] is clear, with 0x12. It brackets the slot callback with norflash_pre_operation_alt (0x0C088898) and norflash_post_operation_alt (0x0C088928), with ble_slot_invoke_callback_evt4 (0x0C08915C) in between. Interrupts are masked with disableIRQinterrupts unless the privileged-mode check reports them already masked. In the masked branch it first writes a debug marker, the return address 0x0C08742E and the link register, to 0x20003D78 and 0x20003D7C, clears the marker afterwards and re-enables interrupts. Returns 0 on success or 10 when the callback fails.

params.name: param_2
params.description: argument passed to the slot callback

returns.description: 0 on success, 10 (0x0A) when the callback fails, 0x12 for a bad id or uninitialised slot

ble_219_0c0873ec.notes: The interpretation of the isIRQinterruptsEnabled result is taken from the branch sense in the code. The debug words suggest a crash-diagnostic marker, which is inferred.

ble_219_0c087464.name: norflash_erase_checked
ble_219_0c087464.summary: Erase a flash slot range after checking that no erase is suspended
ble_219_0c087464.description: Public erase entry. An id above 1, or an uninitialised slot, hangs in an infinite loop (a trap in the binary). If an erase is already suspended (state byte 0x200035B0[id] non-zero) it returns 10. Otherwise it calls ble_slot_get_field_0x14 (0x0C088520) for its side effect, then norflash_erase_range (0x0C086E08) with a zero extra argument and returns that result.

returns.description: result of norflash_erase_range, or 10 when an erase is suspended

ble_219_0c087464.notes: The result of ble_slot_get_field_0x14 is not used by this function in the decompile.

ble_219_0c087cdc.name: norflash_apply_protect_entry
ble_219_0c087cdc.summary: Pick the largest protect-table entry clear of an address range and apply it
ble_219_0c087cdc.description: Works on flash slot 0 only (any other id hangs). If the protect table has entries (count at 0x200038C0), it walks the 3-word entries at 0x200035C0 (SR code, range start, range end). It skips entries that overlap [addr, addr+len) and keeps the largest of the rest, then calls norflash_slot_op_locked (0x0C0873EC) with that entry's SR code. If the call fails it hangs. If no entry qualifies, the initial code 0x7C is left and the function hangs.
ble_219_0c087cdc.notes: The meaning of the SR code and of the entry ordering is inferred from the layout built by norflash_probe_protect_layout.

ble_219_0c087d70.name: norflash_probe_protect_layout
ble_219_0c087d70.summary: Probe a flash slot's JEDEC ID and build its block-protect table
ble_219_0c087d70.description: Runs once per slot, while the flag at 0x200038C4[id] is clear. It reads the first three JEDEC ID bytes with norflash_get_id (0x0C087394) and selects a block-protect layout. Two manufacturer and type patterns are built inline (0xC8 with 0x40 and capacity code 0x12..0x13, and 0x0B with 0x60 and 0x14), writing 3-word entries (SR code, start, end) at 0x200035C0 and the entry count at 0x200038C0. For other IDs it calls the generic builder norflash_build_protect_table (0x0C087A34) when the capacity lies between 64 KiB and just under 32 MiB. The value that norflash_get_id sets at 0x200038C4 scales the block sizes. Unrecognised sizes return or hang.
ble_219_0c087d70.notes: The vendor patterns are matched by the decompiled comparisons only, with no datasheet check. The layout of the table entries is inferred.
